post.description: Creates a `PENDING_PAYMENT` order for the tickets of your hold and a payment session: send the customer to `paymentUrl`. The order expires with the hold (`expiresAt`); releasing or replacing the hold expires it too. A hold has at most one order: checking it out again returns that order with 200. Once the payment result arrives the order is `PROCESSING` and the hold is used up (checking it out again answers 404). Free orders get no `paymentUrl`: they are `PROCESSING` at once and confirmed by the processing job. 403 `email-not-verified` until you verify your email. 404 for unknown holds and other users’ holds. 409 `hold-expired` once the hold has expired; 409 `event-not-on-sale` when the event was unpublished, cancelled or has started. 503 `payment-provider-unavailable` when the provider fails: the order is kept without a `paymentUrl` and the hold stays, so retry the same request.

post.description: Called by the payment provider (`apps/fake-payments`), not by clients. The signature (`X-Payments-Signature: v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>">`, keyed with `PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and `X-Payments-Timestamp` (Unix seconds, within `PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SEC` of the real time, not the test clock) are checked first: 400 `webhook-signature-invalid` otherwise. A valid body is recorded once per event `id`; deliveries of an event already received answer 200 with `duplicate: true` and change nothing. The first result for an unpaid, unexpired order moves it to `PROCESSING` (its tickets are off sale), and a job confirms (`payment.succeeded`) or fails it (`payment.failed`, tickets released) after `JOB_PROCESSING_DELAY_MS`. A success for an expired order, or for an order that already has a result, is recorded as `REFUND_DUE` and never sells tickets.
